answer: Memory-hard admission puzzles make every seat rent RAM: each epoch an identity solves an Argon2 task needing 4 GB held for ten minutes, salted by a fresh beacon so nothing is reusable. Like a quill that must be dipped anew per word, one box can't share memory across heads. Running k identities on one jetty of hardware scales memory to 4k GB, and cedar-solid audits double the size for identities sharing a subnet.
